title: A ventro-temporal area supporting human allocentric representations
authors: Prosper A. Fiave, Giulia Marin, Thibaud Delavy, Adrien Briefer, Patrik Vuilleumier, Ilaria Sani
abstract: Fiave et al. identify a ventro-temporal cortical region that supports allocentric representations in humans. This area exhibits category-general representations of object-centered spatial relationships across diverse stimuli, interacts with fronto-parietal networks during allocentric judgments, and…

title: Divergent co-transmission by a predictive motor circuit modulates auditory processing
authors: Marryn M. Bennett, Han S.J. Cheong, Kaitlyn N. Boone, Farzaan Salman, Jacob D. Ralston, Jenna M. Luthman, Kevin C. Daly, Gwyneth M. Card, Andrew M. Dacks
abstract: As animals behave, their own movements stimulate their sensory systems. Bennett et al. show that co-transmission allows predictive motor circuits to differentially modulate distinct neural networks impacted by the same movements.

title: The dilution effect of stocking and the loss of wildness among North American mallards
authors: Lauren N. McFarland, Joshua I. Brown, Paige A. Byerly, Nancy Rotzel McInerney, Helen F. James, Robert C. Fleischer, Michael P. Schummer, Philip Lavretsky
abstract: Game-farm mallards, a domestic lineage bred for hunting, have been released across North America for over a century to supplement wild populations. Using historical DNA from museum specimens spanning 1800–2020, McFarland et al. demonstrate how interbreeding with released game-farm mallards has funda…

title: Plant cells at the organ surface use mechanical cues to activate a specific growth-control program
authors: Zoe Nemec-Venza, Annamaria Kiss, Nathan German, Simone Bovio, Louise Hughes, Nadine Field, Marjolaine Martin, Claire Lionnet, Tereza Vavrdova, Qiangnan Feng, Freya de Winter, Roman Hudeček, Verena Kriechbaumer, Moritz K. Nowack, Charlotte Kirchhelle
abstract: Nemec-Venza et al. show how mechanical signals, such as tissue tension, can activate gene expression in epidermal cells at the surface of Arabidopsis roots. The expression of the edge-specific growth regulator RAB-A5c in surface cells is needed to control directional growth in the meristem and limit…

title: Reconstruction of speciation by modification of major-effect genes in Petunia
authors: Martina N. Lüthi, Mathilde Chopy, Andrea E. Berardi, Tracey E. Tenreira, Gina Cannarozzi, Chaobin Li, Lea V. Jäggi, Marta Binaghi, Loreta B. Freitas, Marja Timmermans, Cris Kuhlemeier
abstract: By modifying six genes in the hawkmoth-pollinated Petunia axillaris, Lüthi and Chopy et al. reconstructed the evolutionary shift to bee-pollinated P. secreta. The engineered mimic is indistinguishable from P. secreta in visual appearance and pollinator behavioral assays, providing rare, compelling e…

title: Evolution of a core ribosomal innovation in octopus
authors: Rishav Mitra, Richard Han, Trey J. Scott, Anik G. Grearson, Jessica A. Willi, Christina G. Liu, Hyeongju Kim, Michael C. Jewett, Nicholas W. Bellono, Amy S.Y. Lee
abstract: Mitra, Han, Scott, et al. discovered a unique structural adaptation in octopus ribosomes that increases the accuracy of protein synthesis and evolved alongside their elaborate nervous systems.

title: Brassinosteroid and TPD1 signaling pathways redundantly control anther lobe formation in Arabidopsis thaliana
authors: Weiyue Chen, Liming He, Jingjie Zhang, Weiping Li, Ke Xu, Liang Tao, Meizhen Li, Xiaoping Gou, Cheng Zhang, Jia Li
abstract: Chen et al. demonstrate that the BR and TPD1 signaling pathways redundantly control anther lobe formation during early anther development at stages 1–3. The sharply reduced expression of DWF4 at stages 4–6 likely switches these two pathways from functional redundancy to functional divergence in regu…

title: Gustatory function of Aedes aegypti opsins and TRPA1 in avoiding a natural insect repellent
authors: Avinash Chandel, Pratik Dhavan, Anindya Ganguly, Ramandeep Singh, David Aguilar, Zixin Lu, Qitong Chen, Craig Montell
abstract: Chandel et al. show that the flavonoid catechin is a gustatory repellent for arthropods ranging from the mosquito, Aedes aegypti, to the fruit fly, Drosophila melanogaster, and the tick, Ixodes scapularis. The detection of catechin is mediated by TRPA1. In addition, opsins function in rejection of l…

title: Topography of distance-modulated multisensory object location encoding in mouse area RL
authors: Yue Zhang, Uwe Lewin, Alessandro La Chioma, Tobias Bonhoeffer, Mark Hübener
abstract: Zhang et al. show that mouse area RL, part of posterior parietal cortex, organizes visual and whisker representations of near space into a cross-modal topographic map, using external space itself to reconcile divergent sensory coordinates. Distance profoundly shapes this organization, extending beyo…

title: An erratic aerial approach enables mating survival in the cannibalistic killer fly
authors: David Munkvold, Yiyang Wang, Dan R. Chappell, Natalie Hempel de Ibarra, Trevor J. Wardill, Paloma T. Gonzalez-Bellido
abstract: Mating sequences carry risks for species that engage in cannibalism. Munkvold et al. demonstrate that male killer flies, Coenosia attenuata, reduce this risk with an erratic series of aerial jinks. This behavior allows a male to trigger a female pursuit, avoid cannibalism, contact the female safely…

title: Genomic signatures of female exogamy and cultural interaction in a Tang Dynasty patrilineal clan
authors: Yuchun Wang, Huangzhen Huang, Guodong Song, Peng Cao, Jing Ma, Yu Xu, Jiajing Zheng, Hao Ma, Rui Wang, Xiaomin Yang, Haodong Chen, Xinyue Zou, Haifeng He, Le Tao, Wang Shen, Liangliang Hou, Chuan-Chao Wang
abstract: Wang et al. reconstruct a Tang Dynasty elite clan pedigree, revealing how female exogamy introduced West Eurasian ancestry into a patrilineal lineage and shaped genetic and cultural interaction on the frontier.

title: Genomic targets of hurricane-induced selection on clinging performance in an island lizard
authors: Princeton L. Vaughn, Colin M. Donihue, Andrea D. Rummel, Nicolas C. Rochette, Douglas B. Menke, Amber L. Rittgers, Christina E. Sabin, Anna L. Iouchmanov, Aaron H. Griffing, Anthony Herrel, Jason Kolbe, Jonathan Losos, Shane C. Campbell-Staton
abstract: Vaughn et al. show that hurricanes drive parallel genomic selection signatures in island anoles. One candidate locus (hs6st1) is associated with rear toe length. CRISPR disruption reduces hindfoot elements, and shorter rear toes improve clinging ability in high winds, linking extreme-weather selecti…

The results show that accumulations are female-biased, which contrasts with male-biased natural assemblages, thus providing population-scale genetic evidence tha…

title: Making life from scratch
authors: Michael Gross
abstract: A recent attempt at creating artificial cells cobbles together known processes in a crude way but still doesn’t have the spark of life. Meanwhile researchers are getting closer to a convincing model of a self-replicating RNA of the kind that may have started life on Earth.

title: Comparative musicology reborn
authors: W. Tecumseh Fitch
abstract: Darwin, after noting that some form of music is found in humans around the world, famously puzzled over its evolutionary basis, since “neither the enjoyment nor the capacity of producing musical notes are faculties of the least use to man”1. Darwin’s conviction that music is universal was fueled by…

title: Pierre Chambon (1931–2026)
authors: Vincent Laudet
abstract: Vincent Laudet commemorates the life of molecular biologist Pierre Chambon, whose work greatly expanded our understanding of the mechanisms governing eukaryotic gene expression and whose mentorship inspired generations of scientists.

title: Lara Cassidy
authors: Lara Cassidy
abstract: Interview with Lara Cassidy, who uses ancient genomes to study gene flow, population size and social processes in ancient societies at Trinity College Dublin.

title: The mammalian glycocalyx
authors: Ling-Ting Huang, Matthew J. Paszek
abstract: In this Primer, Ling-Ting Huang and Matt Paszek introduce the glycocalyx — the dense carbohydrate-rich layer that coats the external surface of cells — and discuss its composition, structure, biological functions, and relevance to health and pathology.

title: Danionella cerebrum
authors: Xinwei Wang, Tom Baden
abstract: Danionella cerebrum is a tiny, transparent, sexually mature fish emerging as a powerful vertebrate model for whole-organism neuroscience. This primer argues that its promise depends on understanding its unusual size, transparency, ecology and development as biology, not merely as experimental conven…

title: The challenge of decoding animal communication using AI
authors: Mor Taub, Inbal Arnon, Amiyaal Ilany, Mirjam Knörnschild, Yoav Ram, Yossi Yovel
abstract: Animal communication studies often classify signals by their physical similarity, assuming it reflects how animals perceive meaning. Using vocalizations of pre-linguistic toddlers, Taub et al. show that acoustic similarity does not necessarily correlate with the receiver’s perceptual space, highligh…

title: Rapid fine-scale sensorimotor plasticity in human foveal vision
authors: Benjamin Moon, Krishnamachari S. Prahalad, Ashley M. Clark, Austin Roorda, Pavan Tiruveedhula, Wolf Harmening, Aleksandr Gutnikov, Samantha K. Jenks, Sanjana Kapisthalam, Michele Rucci, Jannick P. Rolland, Martina Poletti
abstract: Moon et al. show that a minute foveolar scotoma, invisible to observers, impairs vision and rapidly reorganizes fixation behavior, re-centering stimuli on a new retinal locus. This fine-scale visuomotor plasticity reveals how the eye adapts to subtle central vision loss and may provide an early mark…

title: Multisensory integration: Distance brings the senses together
authors: Philip R.L. Parker
abstract: To act on the world, the brain must fuse vision and touch despite their different formats. A new study finds that egocentric distance organizes this integration across mouse rostrolateral visual area RL, laid out as a single map spanning the visual-to-tactile divide.

title: Plant morphogenesis: Breaking out of the epidermal shell
authors: Rotem Matosevich, Charlotte Kirchhelle
abstract: The epidermis has long been viewed as the main growth-constraining tissue regulating organ shape. A new study challenges this view by showing that internal cell divisions can determine organ size, with the epidermis accommodating the developmental demands.

title: Development: A glial clock coordinates Hedgehog gradients and Notch activity
authors: Nadia Formicola, Filipe Pinto-Teixeira
abstract: How tissues are partitioned into distinct cell types is a fundamental question in development. A new study reveals that glial cells function as a spatiotemporal clock, coordinating a Hedgehog gradient with graded Notch signalling to pattern cell identities at single-cell resolution.

title: Visual cognition: A cortical node for object-centered spatial attention
authors: Franco Pestilli
abstract: Visual attention is often described as the selection of locations in retinal or body-centered space, yet behavior also requires selection within objects. A new study identifies posterior inferotemporal cortex as a ventro-temporal node for object-centered spatial representation.

title: Plant physiology: Coumarin as a regulaTOR of root iron deficiency
authors: Nan Jiang, Karen A. Sanguinet
abstract: Coumarins have long been recognized for their roles in environmental adaptation and iron acquisition. A new study now suggests that the coumarin esculetin may directly inhibit TOR signaling by competing with ATP, linking iron deficiency to growth restriction in plants.

title: Ecophysiology: How pollinators use microclimates determines their thermal risk
authors: H. Arthur Woods, Sylvain Pincebourde
abstract: A study using a deep learning-based system to recognize pollinators suggests pollinating insects decide where to forage based on fine-scale heterogeneity in temperature. These decisions may help some insects to escape the heat while amplifying the thermal risk for others.

title: Conservation: When extremes meet rarity
authors: Siti Nor Baizurah, Vivienne P. Groner
abstract: A catastrophic five-day rain triggered over 50,000 landslides across the core habitat of the critically endangered Tapanuli orangutan in Sumatra, potentially killing a significant proportion of the population and raising urgent questions about rare species' viability in a changing climate.

title: Plant cell biology: Hechtian strands unraveled
authors: Denise S. Arico, Olivier Hamant
abstract: Almost two centuries after their initial description in plants, persistent attachments between the plasma membrane and the cell wall are being revisited. Several recent studies highlight the roles of cellulose synthase, remorin, Feronia, lectin domains and boron crosslinks, and open new research ave…

title: The mechanosensitive protein Zyxin influences Hippo signaling and tissue growth via adherens junctions and basal spot junctions in Drosophila
authors: Harmanjeet Singh, Elliot Brooks, Connor Keegan, Kyoko Jinnai, Shu Kondo, Samuel A. Manning, Benjamin Kroeger, Kieran F. Harvey
abstract: Singh et al. show that the mechanosensitive protein Zyxin (Zyx) localizes to adherens and basal spot junctions of Drosophila epithelia, where it recruits Ajuba and Warts to limit Hippo signaling and promote Yorkie-dependent growth. Zyx also supports the transmission of cytoskeletal tension at these…

title: Mimics of the chordate gut-brain hormone neurotensin in parasitic intestinal hookworms
authors: Thomas Lund Koch, Ho Yan Yeung, Iris Bea L. Ramiro, Joshua P. Torres, Alina Anhnhi Vo, Seph Palomino, Ebbe Engholm, Samuel D. Robinson, Lachlan D. Rash, Zildjian G. Acyatan, Nicholas C. Schumann, Kasper B. Pedersen, Knud J. Jensen, Katrine T. Schjoldager, Amol Patwardhan, Neil D. Young, Michael J. Robertson, Helena Safavi-Hemami
abstract: Using genomics and transcriptomics, Koch, Yeung, et al. identify ancylotensins, a peptide family from parasitic hookworms that mimic the gut hormone neurotensin. Ancylotensins activate host neurotensin receptors and modulate gut function, revealing gut hormone mimicry as a potential mechanism by whi…

title: Transmission heterogeneity emerges from uncoupled parasite shedding and spreading
authors: Luís M. Silva, Dominik Vinopal, Victoria G. Choi, Tommy J. Travers-Cook, Kayla C. King
abstract: Silva et al. show that disease transmission emerges from multiple ecological bottlenecks rather than a single host trait. Separating parasite shedding from downstream infection success reveals why hosts releasing the most parasites are not necessarily those driving disease spread.

title: Sensory processing reallocation from auditory to cardiac signals in REM sleep
authors: Jacinthe Cataldi, Andria Pelentritou, Sophie Schwartz, Marzia De Lucia
abstract: Cataldi, Pelentritou, et al. demonstrated that decreased neural responses to sounds from wakefulness to tonic and phasic REM in human sleep are paralleled by increased responses to heartbeats. A marker based on the auditory to cardiac response ratio captures this shift, offering a behavior-independe…

title: Increased signaling of the Neanderthal growth hormone receptor
authors: Philipp Kanis, Miriam Berreiter, Daniel Sieme, Olivia Wootton, Xiang-Chun Ju, Nicholas E. Holzwart, David Ziliang Hu, Shu Tadaka, Makiko Taira, Kengo Kinoshita, Richard Ågren, Johan G. Olsen, Tomislav Maricic, Hilary C. Martin, Birthe B. Kragelund, Svante Pääbo, Andrew J. Brooks, Hugo Zeberg
abstract: Neanderthals had a robust build, but the genetic basis remains unclear. Kanis et al. show that a Neanderthal growth hormone receptor variant increases cellular growth signaling and is inherited by some present-day humans through archaic admixture. Carriers tend to have more muscle mass and some cran…

title: Global effectiveness of mountain protected areas for biodiversity conservation across elevational gradient
authors: Tao Hu, Dongmei Xu, Xiaoyu Li, Hui Tang, Jiayao Shu, Qiancheng Lv, Yixin Chen, Jian Peng
abstract: Hu et al. find that the mountain protected area effectiveness for biodiversity conservation varies along elevational gradient globally, revealing the limits of area-based conservation and the need for vertical effectiveness.

title: Humpback whales match song production to dive patterns
authors: Julia M. Zeh, Marc O. Lammers, Anke Kügler, Adam A. Pack, Valeria Perez-Marrufo, Maura Schonwald, Susan E. Parks
abstract: Using short-duration tags on humpback whales in Hawai‘i, Zeh et al. find that repeating song components, known as themes, are linked to specific parts of a dive. These results demonstrate the connections between physiology, environment, and behavior in a learned display.

title: Concerted evolution reveals co-adapted amino acid substitutions in Na+K+-ATPase of frogs that prey on toxic toads
authors: Shabnam Mohammadi, Lu Yang, Arbel Harpak, Santiago Herrera-Álvarez, María del Pilar Rodríguez-Ordoñez, Julie Peng, Karen Zhang, Jay F. Storz, Susanne Dobler, Andrew J. Crawford, Peter Andolfatto
